description: Standard TRIGA fuel element (12 wt% U, 20% enriched, U-ZrH1.6) and the core-average moderation ratio of the JSI TRIGA core, from open sources only (no ICSBEP data).

sources.svajger2024: I. Švajger, D. Čalič, A. Pungerčič, A. Trkov, L. Snoj, Evaluation of reactor pulse experiments, Nuclear Engineering and Technology 56 (2024) 1165–1203, doi:10.1016/j.net.2023.11.021 (Table 1; section 4.2)
sources.pnnl2011: R. J. McConn Jr et al., Compendium of Material Composition Data for Radiation Transport Modeling, PNNL-15870 Rev. 1 (2011), stainless steel 304 (fractions typed from memory, NOT checked against the document; cladding composition has a negligible effect on fuel temperature feedback)

gap.source: svajger2024 Table 1 (radius); void is our simplification

cladding.source: svajger2024 Table 1 (density); composition recalled, see sources.pnnl2011

coreAverageCell.source: svajger2024 section 4.2 (active height, radius to the graphite reflector, fuel and water volumes for core 133)
coreAverageCell.note: Equivalent unit cell per fuel element: water area = V_water / (V_fuel / fuel-meat volume per element) / height; cell area = that + the element's outer area. Matches the core-average water-to-fuel ratio, not the grid pitch.

referenceAlpha.source: svajger2024 Table 2 (full 3-D model of core 133, Serpent 2.1.27, ENDF/B-VII.0, fuel temperature only)
referenceAlpha.note: Absolute k is for the whole core and is not comparable with a unit cell; the temperature differences are the comparison target.
